items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: Then I got started, uh, back in the fifties, recording Mineta. He would teach all instruments.

ctx.x: And this is on the New Orleans Ensemble Stock.

Yeah, it must be, uh, these, uh, I had George Gayno on, uh, who was a wonderful talker. I used to transcribe his lessons. About a dozen of his lessons, probably, on banjo. Then I got started, uh, back in the fifties, recording Mineta. He would teach all instruments. And, uh, still I have a chapter. I had Irvin Helfer, a young pianist from Chicago, recorded a lesson or two of his on piano. I would have a chapter by Mineta on the piano in the band, I guess, as they called it. That was another Otis Ferguson article…

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1975-02-02
items.q: And even according to Manuel Mineta, I don't know if I ever talked to anybody else about the make of horn that Bolden used.

ctx.x: So anyway, to get back to the point, Gene Williams had heard these records and agreed with me too that at least Bunk showed some possibilities. You couldn't really tell much how he played, both because his lip wasn't in shape and just by himself. The type of trumpet playing that Bunk did, which was a remarkable thing, and yet by itself it wouldn't sound that effective. Bunk was hardly ever on the beat, so if you didn't hear him patting his foot and all there, you could really tell of course where the beat is, but…
Well, of course, we'll never know what Joe Oliver really sounded like.

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-09-04
items.q: I've seen him walk in white places with, even with me, that nobody would

ctx.x: Yeah. But they'd gone together... Anyway, say, 10 years or so ago, quite a while back. Anyway, George Barquet's brother, Sheil, who wasn't as well-known as George, down here at least, had passed for white for years. I know Mineta says he met him once on Canal Street after he started passing, and he said, well, I like it better. I forget. I have that in some of the Mineta interviews. Some of that stuff I'll copy, too, later on, which is on tape. He likes it better. Mineta sort of, you know, he wasn't mad at him or…
